extracted.intended_audience: applicants/licensees for submarine cable landing licenses and wireless antenna collocations; FCC staff; state historic preservation officers; tribes; tower companies
extracted.subtask_short: submarine cable and antenna collocation compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and procedures governing submarine cable license reporting and streamlining eligibility, FCC electronic filing and application actions, and the Nationwide Programmatic Agreement for collocation of wireless antennas (Section 106 compliance). Includes intergovernmental cooperation procedures under section 410.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly reports — provisioning and maintenance summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Any licensee that is, or is affiliated with, a carrier with market power in any of the cable's destination countries must file quarterly reports summarizing the provisioning and maintenance of all network facilities and services procured from the licensee's affiliate in that destination market, within ninety (90) days from the end of each calendar quarter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports shall contain: (1) the types of facilities and services provided (for example, a lease of wet link capacity in the cable, collocation of licensee's equipment in the cable station with the ability to provide backhaul, or cable station and backhaul services provided to the licensee); (2) for provisioned facilities and services, the volume or quantity provisioned, and the time interval between order and delivery; and (3) the number of outages and intervals between fault report and facility or service restoration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly reports — active and idle circuits
rubrics_metrics.description: Any licensee that is, or is affiliated with, a carrier with market power in any of the cable's destination countries must file quarterly, within 90 days from the end of each calendar quarter, a report of its active and idle 64 kbps or equivalent circuits by facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facility types to be reported include terrestrial, satellite and submarine cable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for streamlining — non-foreign-carrier certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Each applicant must demonstrate eligibility for streamlining by certifying that it is not a foreign carrier and it is not affiliated with a foreign carrier in any of the cable's destination markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This certification is one of several alternative routes to establish streamlining eligibility under §1.70016(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for streamlining — lack of foreign carrier market power
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may demonstrate eligibility for streamlining by demonstrating pursuant to §63.12(c)(1)(i) through (iii) of this chapter that any such foreign carrier or affiliated foreign carrier lacks market power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the demonstrative standards and evidentiary requirements in §63.12(c)(1)(i)-(iii) for establishing lack of market power of a foreign carrier or affiliate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for streamlining — WTO-member destination certification and reporting acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may certify that the destination market where the applicant is, or has an affiliation with, a foreign carrier is a World Trade Organization (WTO) Member and that the applicant agrees to accept and abide by the reporting requirements set out in §1.70015.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application that includes an applicant that is, or is affiliated with, a carrier with market power in a cable's non-WTO Member destination country is not eligible for streamlining.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for streamlining — U.S. ownership/controls certification
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant must certify that all individuals or entities that hold a ten percent or greater direct or indirect equity and/or voting interests, or a controlling interest, in the applicant are U.S. citizens or entities organized in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ownership/voting-interest certification is required to establish eligibility for streamlined processing under §1.70016(a)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for streamlining — CZMA consistency certification / state waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: For a license to construct and operate a submarine cable system or to modify the construction of a previously approved submarine cable system, the applicant must certify that it is not required to submit a consistency certification to any state pursuant to section 1456(c)(3)(A) of the Coastal Zone Management Act (CZMA). Streamlining of cable landing license applications will be limited to those applications where all potentially affected states, having constructive notice that the application was filed with the Commission, have waived, or are deemed to have waived, any section 1456(c)(3)(A) right to review the application within the thirty-day period prescribed by 15 CFR 930.54.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must either certify no CZMA certification is required or rely on state waivers as defined by the CZMA implementing regulations (15 CFR 930.54).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing requirement via ICFS
rubrics_metrics.description: With the exception of submarine cable outage reports, and subject to the availability of electronic forms, all applications and notifications described in this subpart must be filed electronically through the International Communications Filing System (ICFS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A list of available electronic forms can be found on the ICFS homepage. For information on electronic filing requirements see subpart Y of this part and the ICFS homepage (https://www.fcc.gov/icfs). Submarine cable outage reports must be filed as set forth in part 4 of this chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action on applications — Office of International Affairs discretion and due process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of International Affairs shall determine appropriate procedures on a case by case basis for grant or denial of an application or revocation and/or termination of a cable landing license, and grant or deny an application, initiate and conduct application, revocation, and/or termination proceedings, and revoke and/or terminate a cable landing license, as required by due process and applicable law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures should consider relevant facts and circumstances, including providing the applicant or licensee with notice and opportunity to cure noncompliance to the extent required by the Administrative Procedure Act (5 U.S.C. 558(c)), and opportunity to respond to allegations and evidence in the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of institution of proceeding to State commissions (Appendix A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever there shall be instituted before the Federal Commission any proceeding involving the rates of any telephone or telegraph carrier, the State commissions of the States affected thereby will be notified immediately thereof by the Federal Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each notice will advise the State commission that, if it deems the proceeding one which should be considered under cooperative provisions, it should notify the Federal Commission as to the nature of its interest and request a conference, the creation of a joint board, or a joint hearing, indicating its preference and reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: State notification to FCC of proceedings involving FCC-jurisdiction carriers
rubrics_metrics.description: Each State commission should notify the Federal Commission of any proceeding instituted before it involving the toll telephone rates or the telegraph rates of any carrier subject to the jurisdiction of the Federal Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mutual notice facilitates cooperative action under the Plan of Cooperative Procedure when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure governing joint conferences (Appendix A)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Commission will confer with any State commission regarding any matter relating to the regulation of public utilities subject to the jurisdiction of either commission; the commission desiring a conference should notify the other without delay, and the Federal Commission will promptly arrange for a conference inviting all interested State commissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conferences are arranged in such manner as suits the issue and to encourage cooperative relations where in the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure governing matters referred to a board (Appendix A)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Federal Commission determines it is desirable to refer a matter to a board composed of members from affected States, it will request each interested State commission to nominate members, ensure representation (equal unless waived), and issue an order referring the matter that fixes time/place of hearing and defines force/effect and manner of proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rules of practice and procedure adopted by the Federal Commission shall govern the board as far as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure governing joint hearings and cooperating participation (Appendix A)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Federal Commission determines a joint hearing under sec. 410(b) is desirable, it will invite cooperation via the general solicitor of the National Association of Railroad and Utilities Commissioners (NARUC) or directly to State commissions; State commissions will advise whether they will cooperate and by which commissioner; if more than eight States are involved the Association names a cooperating committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed steps include the general solicitor soliciting written advice, the Association president's authority to accept/decline invitations and determine committee size (with executive committee concurrence), and mechanisms for suggesting cooperation when not initially invited by FCC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of cooperating commissioners (Appendix A)
rubrics_metrics.description: In appointing any cooperating committee, the president of the Association shall make appointments only from commissions of the States interested and shall select cooperating commissioners who are especially qualified by reason of ability and fitness and only after confirming practicable availability to attend hearings and conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A cooperating commissioner must commit to be sufficiently informed on the issues and able to form a reasonable judgment in the matters to be determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenure and substitution rules for cooperating commissioners (Appendix A)
rubrics_metrics.description: A commissioner selected to serve on a cooperating committee shall continue to serve in the proceeding until final disposition, provided he/she remains a State commissioner; no member may designate another commissioner to serve in his place; vacancies are filled by the Association president for committees involving more than eight States, or by the commission from which the vacancy occurs for up to eight States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vacancy procedures differ depending on whether the proceeding involves more than eight States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperating committee reporting (Appendix A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a cooperating committee concludes its work or deems it advisable, it shall consider whether to make a report to the interested State commissions; if it determines to make a report, it shall distribute it through the secretary of the association or general solicitor to all interested commissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a report of the Federal Commission accompanies any order, the Federal Commission will state the concurrence or nonconcurrence of the cooperating committee in the decision or order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Antenna' (Appendix B, Stipulation I.A)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Antenna" means an apparatus designed for the purpose of emitting radio frequency ("RF") radiation, to be operated or operating from a fixed location pursuant to FCC authorization, for the transmission of writing, signs, signals, data, images, pictures, and sounds of all kinds, including the transmitting device and any on-site equipment, switches, wiring, cabling, power sources, shelters or cabinets associated with that antenna and added to a Tower, structure, or building as part of the original installation of the antenna.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For purposes of this Agreement, the term Antenna does not include unintentional radiators, mobile stations, or devices authorized under Part 15 of the FCC's rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Collocation' (Appendix B, Stipulation I.B)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Collocation" means the mounting or installation of an antenna on an existing tower, building or structure for the purpose of transmitting and/or receiving radio frequency signals for communications purposes, whether or not there is an existing antenna on the structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Nationwide Programmatic Agreement applies only to collocations as so defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Tower' (Appendix B, Stipulation I.D)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Tower" is any structure built for the sole or primary purpose of supporting FCC-licensed antennas and their associated facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition frames which structures are covered by the collocation agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Substantial increase in the size of the tower' (Appendix B, Stipulation I.E)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Substantial increase in the size of the tower" means any of the following: (1) mounting the proposed antenna would increase the existing height of the tower by more than 10%, or by the height of one additional antenna array with separation from the nearest existing antenna not to exceed twenty feet, whichever is greater; (2) installation of more than the standard number of new equipment cabinets for the technology involved, not to exceed four, or more than one new equipment shelter; (3) adding an appurtenance to the body of the tower that would protrude from the edge of the tower more than twenty feet, or more than the width of the tower structure at the level of the appurtenance; or (4) expanding the boundaries of the current tower site by more than 30 feet in any direction or involving excavation outside these expanded boundaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mounting may exceed size limits where necessary to avoid interference or to shelter the antenna or connect via cable; the current tower site is defined as the current boundaries of the leased or owned property surrounding the tower and any access or utility easements currently related to the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Nationwide Collocation Programmatic Agreement (Appendix B, Stipulation II)
rubrics_metrics.description: This Nationwide Collocation Programmatic Agreement applies only to the collocation of antennas as defined in Stipulations I.A and I.B, and does not cover any Section 106 responsibilities that federal agencies other than the FCC may have with regard to the collocation of antennas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agreement is a program alternative for FCC Section 106 compliance for collocations; other federal agency obligations remain outside its scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collocation on towers constructed on or before March 16, 2001 — Section 106 exemption and exceptions (Appendix B, Stipulation III.A)
rubrics_metrics.description: An antenna may be mounted on an existing tower constructed on or before March 16, 2001 without such collocation being reviewed through the Section 106 process set forth in the NPA, unless: (1) the mounting will result in a substantial increase in the size of the tower as defined in Stipulation I.E; (2) the tower has been determined by the FCC to have an adverse effect on one or more historic properties not avoided or mitigated; (3) the tower is the subject of a pending environmental review or related proceeding before the FCC involving compliance with Section 106; or (4) the collocation licensee or the owner of the tower has received written or electronic notification that the FCC is in receipt of a complaint from a member of the public, an Indian Tribe, a SHPO or the Council, that the collocation has an adverse effect on one or more historic properties, with such complaint in writing and supported by substantial evidence describing how the effect from the collocation is adverse to the attributes that qualify any affected historic property for eligibility or potential eligibility for the National Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where any of these exceptions apply, the collocation is not eligible for the streamlined Section 106 alternative under the Agreement and the standard NPA process or other mitigation/resolution applies.
